Financial regulators in Britain have imposed a rather unusual rule on the bosses of big banks . Starting next year , any guaranteed bonus of top executives could be delayed 10 years if their banks are under investigation for wrongdoing . The main purpose of this “ clawback ” rule is to hold bankers accountable for harmful risk-taking and to restore public trust in financial institution . Yet officials also hope for a much larger benefit : more long term decision-making , not only by banks but also by all corporations , to build a stronger economy for future generations .

“ Short-termism ” or the desire for quick profits , has worsened in publicly traded companies , says the Bank of England ’ s top economist , Andrew Haldane . He quotes a giant of classical economics , Alfred Marshall , in describing this financial impatience as acting like “ Children who pick the plums out of their pudding to eat them at once ” rather than putting them aside to be eaten last .

The average time for holding a stock in both the United States and Britain , he notes , has dropped from seven years to seven months in recent decades . Transient investors , who demand high quarterly profits from companies , can hinder a firm ’s efforts to invest in long-term research or to build up customer loyalty . This has been dubbed “ quarterly capitalism ”.

In addition , new digital technologies have allowed more rapid trading of equities , quicker use of information , and thus shorter attention spans in financial markets . “ There seems to be a predominance of short-term thinking at the expense of long-term investing ,” said Commissioner Daniel Gallagher of the US Securities and Exchange Commission in speech this week .

In the US , the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 has pushed most public companies to defer performance bonuses for senior executives by about a year , slightly helping reduce “ short-termism .” In its latest survey of CEO pay , The Wall Street Journal finds that " a substantial part " of executive pay is now tied to performance .

Much more could be done to encourage “ long-termism ,” such as changes in the tax code and quicker disclosure of stock acquisitions . In France , shareholders who hold onto a company investment for at least two years can sometimes earn more voting rights in a company .

Within companies , the right compensation design can provide incentives for executives to think beyond their own time at the company and on behalf of all stakeholders . Britain ’s new rule is a reminder to bankers that society has an interest in their performance , not just for the short term but for the long term .

C. build a new system of financial regulation

【偷换概念】C. 建立一种新的金融监管系统：1段1句中提到，英国的金融监管机构对大型银行的高管实施了一项非同寻常的规定，并未提及要建立一种新的金融监管系统，故排除。

【反向干扰】D. 保证高管人员的奖金：1段2句中提到，新规定实施后，银行不当行为可能导致高管人员的奖金延迟十年发放，可见实施新规定并不是为了保证高管人员的奖金，故排除。

我们来看第一段第三句话，里面明确说：“The main purpose of the new rule is to hold bankers accountable for harmful risk-taking and to restore public trust in financial institutions.” 翻译过来就是：这项新规的主要目的是让银行家为他们所冒的有害风险负责，并恢复公众对金融机构的信任。这里有两个目的，但题干只要求“one motive”，所以只要选项匹配其中一点就行。

现在看选项，A 选项“增强银行家的责任意识”，其实就是对“hold bankers accountable for harmful risk-taking”的通俗说法——让银行家对自己的高风险行为负责，自然就要求他们更有责任感。所以 A 是对原文意思的合理转述，是正确答案。

再来看看其他选项为什么不对。B 选项说“帮助企业赚更多钱”，但原文压根没提利润或者企业收益，完全是无中生有，可以直接排除。C 选项“建立新的金融监管体系”听起来挺高大上，但原文只说了一项具体的新规，并没有说要整个重建监管系统，属于夸大范围、偷换概念。D 选项更离谱，说是为了“保证高管奖金”，而原文恰恰是在限制那些因冒险行为拿高额奖金的做法，所以 D 不仅不对，还和文意相反。

Starting next year , any guaranteed bonus of top executives could be delayed 10 years if their banks are under investigation for wrongdoing . The main purpose of this “ clawback ” rule is to hold bankers accountable for harmful risk-taking and to restore public trust in financial institution . Yet officials also hope for a much larger benefit : more long term decision-making , not only by banks but also by all corporations , to build a stronger economy for future generations .

“ Short-termism ” or the desire for quick profits , has worsened in publicly traded companies , says the Bank of England ’ s top economist , Andrew Haldane . He quotes a giant of classical economics , Alfred Marshall , in describing this financial impatience as acting like “ Children who pick the plums out of their pudding to eat them at once ” rather than putting them aside to be eaten last .

The average time for holding a stock in both the United States and Britain , he notes , has dropped from seven years to seven months in recent decades . Transient investors , who demand high quarterly profits from companies , can hinder a firm ’s efforts to invest in long-term research or to build up customer loyalty . This has been dubbed “ quarterly capitalism ”.

In addition , new digital technologies have allowed more rapid trading of equities , quicker use of information , and thus shorter attention spans in financial markets . “ There seems to be a predominance of short-term thinking at the expense of long-term investing ,” said Commissioner Daniel Gallagher of the US Securities and Exchange Commission in speech this week .

In the US , the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 has pushed most public companies to defer performance bonuses for senior executives by about a year , slightly helping reduce “ short-termism .” In its latest survey of CEO pay , The Wall Street Journal finds that " a substantial part " of executive pay is now tied to performance .

Much more could be done to encourage “ long-termism ,” such as changes in the tax code and quicker disclosure of stock acquisitions . In France , shareholders who hold onto a company investment for at least two years can sometimes earn more voting rights in a company .

Within companies , the right compensation design can provide incentives for executives to think beyond their own time at the company and on behalf of all stakeholders . Britain ’s new rule is a reminder to bankers that society has an interest in their performance , not just for the short term but for the long term .
2019-Traditional Reading-1-4.analysis:
【题目及选项概览】

The US and France examples are used to illustrate____________.

美国和法国的例子被用来说明________.

A. the obstacles to preventing “short-termism”.

   预防“短期效益主义”所面临的障碍

B. the significance of long-term thinking.

   长期思维的重要性

C. the approaches to promoting “long-termism”.

   推行“长期效益主义”的方式

D. the prevalence of short-term thinking.

   短期思维的盛行


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的US and France examples可以定位至5、6段。5段提到了美国的班克萨斯—奥克斯利法案以及它对遏制“短期效益主义”起到的作用，6段提到在鼓励“长期效益主义”方面，我们还能做很多，接着引用法国的例子具体说明如何鼓励股票持有者践行“长期效益主义”，由此可知，美国和法国都为鼓励推行“长期效益主义”采取了相关措施。

技巧：例证题考查的是例子所论证的论点，所以例子本身不重要，例子所论证的论点更为重要，且常为正确答案。故对于本题而言，5段为例子本身，论点为“遏制短期效益主义”，6段中为基于例证总结归纳的论点为，即鼓励“长效收益主义”能做的事情，故C选项（推行“长期效益主义”的方式）为合理总结归纳。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A. 预防短期效益主义所面临的障碍：文中并未提及预防短期效益主义面临的障碍。

【答非所问】B. 长期思维的重要性：1段4句中提到政府期望通过制定长期决策为后代建设经济更强大的国家，由此可知长期思维的确很重要，但这与美国和法国的示例无关，为答非所问选项。

【答非所问】D. 短期思维的盛行：4段2句中，美国证券交易委员会的丹尼尔指出，短期思维似乎占据了主导地位，这只能说明短期思维在美国证券交易中很盛行，与美国和法国的例子无关，为答非所问选项。
2019-Traditional Reading-1-4.tips:
这道题问的是美国和法国的例子被用来说明什么，属于典型的“例证题”。做这类题的关键在于：**例子本身不是重点，重点是它要支撑的观点**。很多同学容易掉进陷阱，只盯着例子细节选答案，结果选偏了。


我们先回到原文找定位。题干提到“US and France examples”，顺着这个线索，可以快速锁定文章第5段和第6段。第5段讲的是美国通过《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》来限制企业过度追求短期利润；第6段则转向法国，说那里的法律鼓励股东长期持股，比如对持有股票超过两年的投资者给予更多投票权。这两个例子看似不同，但其实都在讲同一件事：**各国正在用具体政策或制度设计，来推动“长期主义”（long-termism）**。


这时候就要注意选项的细微差别了。A选项说的是“预防短期主义的障碍”，但原文并没有强调“障碍”——相反，它在讲“已经采取了哪些有效做法”，所以A不对。B选项“长期思维的重要性”听起来挺有道理，但它太笼统了，而且原文的重点不是“重要性”，而是“怎么做”。D选项说“短期思维很普遍”，这虽然可能是事实，但例子的目的不是为了证明它“普遍存在”，而是展示如何应对它。


再看C选项：“推行‘长期效益主义’的方式”。这正好对应了两个国家的具体做法：美国用法规约束财报透明度，法国用激励机制鼓励长期持股。它们都是实际的操作手段，而不是空谈理念。所以C才是对例子背后论点的准确概括。


这里有个实用技巧：遇到例证题，不妨先跳过例子本身，往前或往后找一句总结性的话。比如第6段开头就说：“There is plenty more that could be done to encourage long-termism.”（还有很多事情可以做来鼓励长期主义）——这句话就是作者真正想表达的观点，而美法两国的例子，正是为这句话服务的。抓住这个“观点句”，答案自然就清晰了。

2019-Traditional Reading-1-5.analysis:
【题目及选项概览】

Which of the following would be the best title for the text?

下列那一个选项是本文的最佳标题？

A. Failure of Quarterly Capitalism

   季度资本主义的失败

B. Patience as a Corporate Virtue

   耐心是公司的美德

C. Decisiveness Required of Top Executives

   高管人员需要决断力

D. Frustration of Risk-taking Bankers

   冒险银行家面临的挫败感


【定位及答案】

本位为主旨题，考查合适的文章标题，需重点阅读全文首末段以及各段首末句。1段提到，英国金融监管机构对银行高管推行了一项新规定；2-4段具体阐述实行新规定的原因，即应对“短期效益主义”的盛行；5-6段提到了美国法国就推行“长期效益主义”采取的具体策略；7段再次强调社会不仅关注银行家们的短期绩效，还关注长期绩效。文章主要围绕金融投资展开，强调长期投资和长远打算的重要性。鼓励投资者对投资保持耐心，不要过于急躁，只看眼前利益。B选项（耐心是公司的美德）是对文章的合理概括。


【错选分析】

【以偏概全】A. 季度资本主义的失败：3段提到季度资本主义是短期效益主义的一种，作为短期效益主义盛行的论据出现，非文章讨论主体，以偏概全。

【无中生有】C. 高管人员需要决断力：文中并未提及。

【无中生有】D. 冒险银行家面临的挫败感：文中并未提及。
2019-Traditional Reading-1-5.tips:
这道题问的是“以下哪个选项最适合作为文章的标题”，也就是要我们抓住整篇文章的核心主旨。做这类题，千万别急着看选项，先快速回顾一下文章整体在讲什么——尤其是开头和结尾段，以及每段的首尾句，因为作者通常会在这些地方埋下主线。


通读全文你会发现，文章一开始提到英国金融监管机构出台了一项新规，要求银行高管的奖金不能马上兑现，而是要等好几年。乍一看好像是在“惩罚”银行家，但往下读就会明白，这其实是在对抗一种普遍存在的“短期主义”思维——很多公司只盯着每个季度的财报数据，为了眼前利益牺牲长远发展。作者接着用“季度资本主义”（quarterly capitalism）这个词来形容这种现象，并指出它带来的问题。


后面几段进一步展开：美国和法国都在尝试推动“长期主义”策略，比如让投资者更关注企业五到十年的发展，而不是下一季度赚多少钱。最后一段更是点明：社会对银行家的期待，不只是短期业绩亮眼，更要看他们能否为未来打下基础。所以整篇文章其实在呼吁一种耐心、长远的眼光，尤其是在企业决策和投资行为中。


现在来看选项，B项“Patience as a Corporate Virtue”（耐心是公司的美德）正好精准概括了这个主旨。这里的“corporate”不单指银行或金融行业，而是泛指企业界；“virtue”（美德）也呼应了文章把“耐心”当作一种值得推崇的价值观来倡导。


其他选项为什么不对？A项“季度资本主义的失败”听起来很相关，但它只是文章用来说明问题的一个例子或现象，并不是全文要讨论的核心观点——就像用“发烧”来说明生病了，但文章重点不是发烧本身，而是整个健康问题。C项和D项就更离谱了，文中压根没提“高管需要决断力”或者“银行家感到挫败”，属于典型的无中生有，是命题人故意设置的干扰项。


这里提醒大家一个常见陷阱：主旨题最容易错选成“细节放大版”。看到某个词在文中出现过（比如“quarterly capitalism”），就以为它是重点。其实，标题必须能覆盖全文，而不是只罩住某一段。判断标准很简单：如果去掉这个选项，文章还能不能完整表达它的主要思想？如果答案是否定的，那它就不是主旨。

2019-Traditional Reading-2-1.article:
Grade inflation — the gradual increase in average GPAs ( grade-point averages ) over the past few decades — is often considered a product of a consumer era in higher education , in which students are treated like customers to be pleased . But another , related force — a policy often buried deep in course catalogs called “ grade forgiveness ”— is helping raise GPAs .

Grade forgiveness allows students to retake a course in which they received a low grade, and the most recent grade or the highest grade is the only one that counts in calculating a student ’s overall GPA .

The use of this little-known practice has accelerated in recent years , as colleges continue to do their utmost to keep students in school ( and paying tuition ) and improve their graduation rates . When this practice first started decades ago , it was usually limited to freshmen , to give them a second chance to take a class in their first year if they struggled in their transition to college-level courses . But now most colleges save for many selective campuses , allow all undergraduates , and even graduate students , to get their low grades forgiven .

College officials tend to emphasize that the goal of grade forgiveness is less about the grade itself and more about encouraging students to retake courses critical to their degree program and graduation without incurring a big penalty . " Ultimately ," said Jack Miner , Ohio State University ’s registrar ," we see students achieve more success because they retake a course and do better in subsequent courses or master the content that allows them to graduate on time ."

That said, there is a way in which grade forgiveness satisfies colleges ’ own needs as well . For public institutions , state funds are sometimes tied partly to their success on metrics such as graduation rates and student retention — so better grades can , by boosting figures like those, mean more money . And anything that raises GPAs will likely make students — who, at the end of the day , are paying the bill — feel they ’ve gotten a better value for their tuition dollars , which is another big concern for colleges .

Indeed , grade forgiveness is just another way that universities are responding to consumers ’ expectations for higher education . Since students and parents expect a college degree to lead to a job , it is in the best interest of a school to turn out graduates who are as qualified as possible — or at least appear to be . On this , students ' and colleges ' incentives seem to be aligned .
2019-Traditional Reading-2-1.analysis:
【题目及选项概览】

What is commonly regarded as the cause of grade inflation?

什么常被视为分数膨胀的原因？

A. The change of course catalogs.

   课程目录的改变

B. Students’ indifference to GPAS.

   学生对平均绩点的漠视

C. Colleges’ neglect of GPAS.

   大学对学生学生平均绩点的忽视

D. The influence of consumer culture.

   消费文化的影响


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的关键词grade inflation、cause、commonly可以定位至1段1句，1段1句中提到，分数膨胀现象被认为是高等教育消费时代的产物，在这个时代，学生被当做顾客来取悦。可见分数膨胀现象的出现是高等教育受到消费文化影响的结果。故D选项（消费文化的影响）为正确选项。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰，偷换概念】A. 课程目录的改变：course catalog出现在1段2句中的but转折后，转折前is often considered=commonly，为一般情况下认为的原因，but后转折为隐含的原因，为反向干扰，且2句指出，通常深藏于课程目录中的“成绩宽容”政策也在助推GPAs的提高，并未提及课程目录的改变。

【无中生有】B. 学生对平均绩点的模式：定位段（1段）中并未提及。

【无中生有】C. 大学对学生平均绩点的忽视：定位段（1段）中并未提及。
2019-Traditional Reading-2-1.tips:
这道题问的是“什么常被视为分数膨胀的原因？”——注意题干里的commonly regarded as，这是关键信号，说明我们要找的是“普遍被认为”的原因，而不是作者个人观点或深层分析。

回到原文第一段开头，作者一上来就说：“Grade inflation—the gradual increase in average GPAs over the decades—is often considered a product of a consumer era in higher education.” 这句话直接对应题干：其中often considered就等于题干中的commonly regarded as，而后面说的a product of a consumer era（消费时代的产物）正是我们要找的答案线索。再往下看，“in which students are treated like customers to be pleased”进一步解释了这种消费文化的特点——学生被当成顾客来讨好，自然老师就不敢给低分，于是分数越来越高。

所以，正确选项必须体现“消费文化的影响”，也就是选项D。这个选项不是在讲某个具体政策或学生态度，而是点出了整个高等教育环境的变化根源，和原文高度吻合。

其他几个选项乍看有点迷惑，但仔细一想就站不住脚。比如A选项说“课程目录的改变”，其实原文提到的是课程目录里隐藏着“成绩宽容”政策，并不是说目录本身变了；而且这句话出现在but之后，是用来补充说明的次要信息，不是“普遍认为”的主要原因。B和C更离谱——文章压根没说学生不在乎GPA，也没说大学忽视GPA，反而是大家都太在乎了，才导致分数越给越高。这两个选项属于典型的“无中生有”，千万别被带偏。

做这类题有个小技巧：看到题干里有commonly, generally, traditionally这类词，就一定要去找原文中表示“普遍看法”的表达，比如often considered, widely believed, many think等，而不是作者的批判或深层分析。考研英语特别喜欢在这种“表面共识”和“作者观点”之间设陷阱，一定要分清！

【题目及选项概览】

What was the original purpose of grade forgiveness?

“成绩宽恕”最初的目的是什么？

A. To help freshmen adapt to college learning.

  帮助大一新生适应大学的学习

B. To maintain colleges’ graduation rates.

  保持大学毕业率

C. To prepare graduates for a challenging future.

  使毕业生做好准备，迎接充满挑战的未来

D. To increase universities’ income from tuition.

  增加大学的学费收入


【定位及答案】

【答非所问】B 保持大学毕业率：3段1句中提到高校继续竭尽全力让学生支付学费和提高毕业率，但这并非成绩宽容政策的初衷，故排除。

Grade inflation — the gradual increase in average GPAs ( grade-point averages ) over the past few decades — is often considered a product of a consumer era in higher education , in which students are treated like customers to be pleased . But another , related force — a policy often buried deep in course catalogs called “ grade forgiveness ”— is helping raise GPAs .

Grade forgiveness allows students to retake a course in which they received a low grade, and the most recent grade or the highest grade is the only one that counts in calculating a student ’s overall GPA .

The use of this little-known practice has accelerated in recent years , as colleges continue to do their utmost to keep students in school ( and paying tuition ) and improve their graduation rates . When this practice first started decades ago , it was usually limited to freshmen , to give them a second chance to take a class in their first year if they struggled in their transition to college-level courses . But now most colleges save for many selective campuses , allow all undergraduates , and even graduate students , to get their low grades forgiven .

College officials tend to emphasize that the goal of grade forgiveness is less about the grade itself and more about encouraging students to retake courses critical to their degree program and graduation without incurring a big penalty . " Ultimately ," said Jack Miner , Ohio State University ’s registrar ," we see students achieve more success because they retake a course and do better in subsequent courses or master the content that allows them to graduate on time ."

That said, there is a way in which grade forgiveness satisfies colleges ’ own needs as well . For public institutions , state funds are sometimes tied partly to their success on metrics such as graduation rates and student retention — so better grades can , by boosting figures like those, mean more money . And anything that raises GPAs will likely make students — who, at the end of the day , are paying the bill — feel they ’ve gotten a better value for their tuition dollars , which is another big concern for colleges .

Indeed , grade forgiveness is just another way that universities are responding to consumers ’ expectations for higher education . Since students and parents expect a college degree to lead to a job , it is in the best interest of a school to turn out graduates who are as qualified as possible — or at least appear to be . On this , students ' and colleges ' incentives seem to be aligned .

【题目及选项概览】

According to Paragraph 5, grade forgiveness enable colleges to_________.

根据第五段的内容，“成绩宽恕”使大学得以________.

A. obtain more financial support

   获得更多的财政资助

B. boost their student enrollments

   增加学生入学人数

C. improve their teaching quality

   提高教学质量

D. meet local governments’ needs

   满足地方政府的需求


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的定位提示信息可以定位至5段①②句，①句提到，成绩宽容政策也成为满足大学自身需要的一种方式，②句提到，国家拨款优势部分取决于公立大学在诸如毕业率以及学生保留率等指标上的良好表现，而更好的成绩有助于提升这些指标的数值，也意味着有更多的资金注入。由此可知，成绩宽容政策可以帮助学校提升诸如毕业率和学生保留率等指标，从而获得更多的国家拨款，也就是A选项中的提到的financial support（财政支持），故A选项为原文的合理推理，为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】B. 增加入学人数：该选项利用5段②句设置感染，②句中的student retention是指政府资金相关的对于学校评价的指标，是指学生的保留率，和增加学校的入学人数无关，为偷换概念选项，故排除。

【无中生有&常识干扰】C. 提高教学质量：该选项在文中定位处并未提及，也属于常识干扰，我们常会认为提升教学质量和学校的整体提升有关，但其和本题所问的问题无关。

【偷换概念】D. 满足地方政府的需求：5段①具体到，成绩宽容政策可以满足的是大学自身的需求，而不是当地政府的需求，故排除。
2019-Traditional Reading-2-3.tips:
这道题问的是“成绩宽恕”（grade forgiveness）让大学能够做什么，关键是要回到原文第五段找线索。很多同学一看到“宽恕成绩”，可能会下意识觉得这是为了学生好，但考研英语阅读常常考的是“背后的利益逻辑”——所以得留意作者有没有提到学校这么做其实是为了自己。

第五段开头就说，grade forgiveness has become a way for colleges to meet their own needs（成绩宽恕已成为大学满足自身需求的一种方式）。这句话就是题眼！它直接告诉我们：这个政策不是单纯为了学生，而是对学校有利。那具体有什么利呢？接着往下看，第二句解释了原因：State funding is partly based on how well public universities perform on metrics like graduation rates and student retention（州政府拨款部分取决于公立大学在毕业率和学生保留率等指标上的表现）。

这里要注意一个关键点：student retention 不是“招生人数”，而是“留住学生”的比例，也就是有多少学生没退学、顺利读下去了。而更好的成绩能提高这些指标——因为如果学生挂科少、GPA高，就更可能按时毕业、不辍学。这样一来，学校的“表现数据”就好看了，政府一看：“不错，值得多给钱！”于是更多财政支持（financial support）就来了。

所以正确选项 A “获得更多的财政资助”其实是对原文逻辑的合理推导。这里用了一个常见的考研阅读技巧：答案往往不是原文原词复现，而是对因果链条的总结。原文没直接说“get more money”，但通过“funding depends on performance → grade forgiveness boosts performance → therefore more funding”这个链条，就能推出 A 正确。

再来看其他选项为什么错。B 说“增加入学人数”，但原文根本没提招生（enrollment），只说了 retention（保留率），这是两个完全不同的概念——把“留住老生”偷换成“招来新生”是典型陷阱。C 选项“提高教学质量”听起来很正面，但全文没说成绩宽恕跟教学水平有任何关系，纯属主观联想。D 选项“满足地方政府需求”看似沾边，但原文说的是大学为了拿钱去迎合评估指标，而不是主动配合政府的政策目标，方向反了。

总结一下：遇到这种“某措施使机构得以……”的题目，一定要盯住原文中关于动机或利益的表述，别被表面善意迷惑。同时，警惕选项里那些看起来合理但原文没提的“美好愿望”——考研英语考的是证据，不是想象。

【题目及选项概览】

What does the phrase “to be aligned”(Line 5, Para6) most probably mean?

短语“to be aligned”（6段5行）最有可能是什么意思？

A. To counterbalance each other.  互相制衡

B. To complement each other.  互相补充

C. To be identical with each other.  彼此一致

D. To be contradictory to each other.  互相矛盾


【定位及答案】

根据题干提示信息，可以定位至6段3句及其上下句，即6段2、3句。其中3句提到，在这一点上，大学生和大学的动机似乎…，根据分析，该部分的this应指2句中的内容，即学生和家长都希望大学文凭能带来一份工作，二学校也希望培养出尽可能合格或者至少看上去合格的毕业生以使利益最大化，由此可知，学生和学校都有着相同的动机，C选项（彼此一致）为正确选项。


【错选分析】

A（互相制衡）、B（互相补充）、D（互相矛盾） 三个选项都与文中表达的“共同的动机”含义不符，故排除。
2019-Traditional Reading-2-4.tips:
这道题问的是第六段第五行出现的短语“to be aligned”最可能是什么意思。很多同学一看到这种短语题就有点慌，其实只要回到原文、结合上下文，就能轻松搞定。

首先，我们要找到这句话所在的完整语境。原文第六段第三句说：“On this point, the motivations of students and universities appear to be aligned.”（在这一点上，学生和大学的动机似乎是 aligned 的。）这里的“this point”很关键，它指代的是前一句的内容——也就是第二句讲的：学生和家长都希望大学文凭能换来一份好工作，而大学也希望培养出看起来“合格”的毕业生，从而提升自己的声誉和收益。

换句话说，学生想靠文凭找工作，学校也想靠“产出就业率高的毕业生”来吸引生源，双方其实在同一个目标上使劲。这时候再看“aligned”这个词，它原本有“排成一行”“方向一致”的意思，在这里显然不是字面意义，而是比喻双方的动机一致、目标相同。

四个选项中，C. To be identical with each other（彼此一致）最贴近这个意思。注意，这里说的“一致”不是指完全一模一样，而是指在关键目标上没有冲突、方向相同，这正是考研英语常考的“语境义”而非“字典义”。

至于其他选项：A项“互相制衡”暗示对抗关系，B项“互相补充”强调功能上的配合，D项“互相矛盾”更是直接对立——这些都和原文描述的“双方都想通过文凭实现各自利益”的和谐状态不符。尤其要警惕B选项，有些同学会觉得“学生和学校各取所需”就是互补，但原文强调的是动机重合，而不是分工合作。

一个小技巧：遇到短语题，别急着查词典，先看它前后有没有解释性内容或逻辑信号词（比如 here, this, thus 等）。像这里的“on this point”就是明显的指代线索，顺着它往前找，答案自然浮现。

【题目及选项概览】

The author examines the practice of grade forgiveness by________.

作者通过________的方式剖析了“成绩宽恕”这一做法。

A. assessing its feasibility

   评估其可行性

B. analyzing the causes behind it

   分析其背后的原因

C. comparing different views on it

   比较对其不同的观点

D. listing its long-run effects

   罗列其长期影响


【定位及答案】

本题非典型的主旨题，但是根据题干内容“作者通过…来探讨“成绩宽容”政策的实施”，并根据前文阅读可以发现，全文各处多次出现grade forgiveness，可以推测，本题考查的作者如何探讨该政策的实施需要对全文篇章结构进行分析。文章1、2段通过分数膨胀现象引出话题，即高校的成绩宽容政策；3、4段指出成绩宽容政策实施的初衷与目的，5段从高校角度分析了成绩宽容政策实施的原因；6段指出成绩宽容政策的实质。可见，作者通过分析成绩宽容政策实施背后的原因来探讨该政策的实施，故B选项（分析其背后的原因）为正确选项。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A. 评估其可行性：原文分析并未提及其可行性分析。

【以偏概全，曲解文意】C. 比较对其不同的观点：4段中College officials和Jack Miner 表明了对于成绩宽容政策的肯定；6段2句中提到了students and parents 对大学文凭能带来一份工作的期望，这并非他们对成绩宽容政策实施的观点，由此可知，作者并未比较不同人对成绩宽容政策实施的不同观点，故C选项为以偏概全曲解文意选项。

【偷换概念】D. 罗列其长期影响：4、5段虽然体积成绩宽容政策对学生和学校的积极影响，但并未说明其产生了长期影响，故排除。
2019-Traditional Reading-2-5.tips:
这道题问的是：作者是通过什么方式来探讨“成绩宽恕”（grade forgiveness）这一做法的。很多同学一看到这种题，容易直接去回忆文章讲了什么内容，但其实关键在于作者是怎么展开论述的，也就是他的写作手法或思路。


我们回看全文结构会发现，文章开头先提到一个现象——高校普遍存在“分数膨胀”，然后顺势引出“成绩宽恕”这个具体政策。接着，作者并没有停留在表面描述，而是深入一层，开始解释为什么学校要推行这项政策。比如第三、四段讲到，学校希望借此提升学生GPA、增强他们的自信心；第五段更进一步，从学校的立场出发，指出这种做法其实也和招生竞争、学生满意度等现实利益挂钩。


换句话说，作者不是在评估这个政策好不好用（那就涉及可行性了），也不是单纯罗列它带来哪些长期后果，更没有花大量篇幅对比不同人对它的看法。整篇文章的主线非常清晰：不断追问“为什么会这样”——为什么学校愿意让学生重修课程并覆盖原成绩？背后有哪些教育理念或现实动因？这种层层递进的“原因分析”正是作者剖析该政策的核心方式。


这时候再看选项，B项“分析其背后的原因”就完全契合了。而其他选项呢？A项“评估可行性”属于典型的无中生有——文章压根没讨论这个政策能不能落地；C项“比较不同观点”看似合理，但通篇其实是以作者视角为主导，并未呈现对立或多元立场的交锋；D项“罗列长期影响”也不对，虽然第六段提到了一些后果，但那只是服务于整体论证的一小部分，远非全文重心。


这里提醒大家一个常见陷阱：考研英语阅读中，如果题目问的是“作者如何探讨某事”，重点不在“说了什么”，而在“怎么说的”。别被细节带偏，一定要抓住行文逻辑和论证主线。像本题，只要意识到作者始终在挖掘“动机”和“成因”，答案自然就浮出来了。

2019-Traditional Reading-3-1.article:
This year marks exactly two centuries since the publication of Frankenstein ; or , The Modern Prometheus , by Mary Shelley . Even before the invention of the electric light bulb , the author produced a remarkable work of speculative fiction that would foreshadow many ethical questions to be raised by technologies yet to come .

Today the rapid growth of artificial intelligence ( AI ) raises fundamental questions :" What is intelligence , identity , or consciousness ?" What makes humans humans

What is being called artificial general intelligence , machines that would imitate the way humans think , continues to evade scientists . Yet humans remain fascinated by the idea of robots that would look , move, and respond like humans , similar to those recently depicted on popular sci-fi TV series such as " West world " and " Humans ".

Just how people think is still far too complex to be understood , let alone reproduced , says David Eagleman , a Stanford University neuroscientist . " We are just in a situation where there are no good theories explaining what consciousness actually is and how you could ever build a machine to get there ."

But that doesn’t mean crucial ethical issues involving AI aren’t at hand . The coming use of autonomous vehicles , for example , poses thorny ethical questions . Human drivers sometimes must make split-second decisions . Their reactions may be a complex combination of instant reflexes , input from past driving experiences , and what their eyes and ears tell them in that moment . AI " vision " today is not nearly as sophisticated as that of humans . And to anticipate every imaginable driving situation is a difficult programming problem .

Whenever decisions are based on masses of data , " you quickly get into a lot of ethical questions ," notes Tan Kiat How , chief executive of a Singapore-based agency that is helping the government develop a voluntary code for the ethical use of AI . Along with Singapore , other governments and mega-corporations are beginning to establish their own guidelines . Britain is setting up a data ethics center . India released its AI ethics strategy this spring .

On June 7 Google pledged not to " design or deploy AI " that would cause " overall harm ," or to develop AI-directed weapons or use AI for surveillance that would violate international norms . It also pledged not to deploy AI whose use would violate international laws or human rights .

While the statement is vague , it represents one starting point . So does the idea that decisions made by AI systems should be explainable , transparent , and fair .

To put it another way : How can we make sure that the thinking of intelligent machines reflects humanity ’s highest values Only then will they be useful servants and not Frankenstein ’s out-of-control monster .

【定位及答案】

总结一下解题技巧：遇到开头举例题，别纠结例子本身，赶紧往后看——作者真正想说的观点通常就在例子后面一两句。而且，正确选项往往不会照搬原文词，而是用同义转述表达“功能”或“目的”，比如这里的“involves concerns”就是对“foreshadowed ethical dilemmas”的巧妙改写。

This year marks exactly two centuries since the publication of Frankenstein ; or , The Modern Prometheus , by Mary Shelley . Even before the invention of the electric light bulb , the author produced a remarkable work of speculative fiction that would foreshadow many ethical questions to be raised by technologies yet to come .

Today the rapid growth of artificial intelligence ( AI ) raises fundamental questions :" What is intelligence , identity , or consciousness ?" What makes humans humans

What is being called artificial general intelligence , machines that would imitate the way humans think , continues to evade scientists . Yet humans remain fascinated by the idea of robots that would look , move, and respond like humans , similar to those recently depicted on popular sci-fi TV series such as " West world " and " Humans ".

Just how people think is still far too complex to be understood , let alone reproduced , says David Eagleman , a Stanford University neuroscientist . " We are just in a situation where there are no good theories explaining what consciousness actually is and how you could ever build a machine to get there ."

But that doesn’t mean crucial ethical issues involving AI aren’t at hand . The coming use of autonomous vehicles , for example , poses thorny ethical questions . Human drivers sometimes must make split-second decisions . Their reactions may be a complex combination of instant reflexes , input from past driving experiences , and what their eyes and ears tell them in that moment . AI " vision " today is not nearly as sophisticated as that of humans . And to anticipate every imaginable driving situation is a difficult programming problem .

Whenever decisions are based on masses of data , " you quickly get into a lot of ethical questions ," notes Tan Kiat How , chief executive of a Singapore-based agency that is helping the government develop a voluntary code for the ethical use of AI . Along with Singapore , other governments and mega-corporations are beginning to establish their own guidelines . Britain is setting up a data ethics center . India released its AI ethics strategy this spring .

On June 7 Google pledged not to " design or deploy AI " that would cause " overall harm ," or to develop AI-directed weapons or use AI for surveillance that would violate international norms . It also pledged not to deploy AI whose use would violate international laws or human rights .

While the statement is vague , it represents one starting point . So does the idea that decisions made by AI systems should be explainable , transparent , and fair .

To put it another way : How can we make sure that the thinking of intelligent machines reflects humanity ’s highest values Only then will they be useful servants and not Frankenstein ’s out-of-control monster .

【题目及选项概览】

In David Eagleman’s opinion, our current knowledge of consciousness _______.

大卫·伊格曼认为，我们目前对意识的认识_________。

A. helps explain artificial intelligence.

   有助于解释人工智能

B. can be misleading to robot making.

   可能会对机器人制造造成误导

C. inspires popular sci-fi TV series.

   给流行的科幻电视连续剧带来灵感

D. is too limited for us to reproduce it.

   太有限而无法复制


【定位及答案】

根据定位词David Eagleman可以定位至4段的1、2句；1句中提到大卫认为，人类的思维方式仍然过于复杂，令人难以理解，更不用说复制了；2句则对此观点进行进一步的解释，指出我们目前还没有好的理论来解释意识到底是什么，以及如何制造出一台达到人类意识水平的机器。可见，大卫认为，我们对于人类意识的人士还不足，以至于无法复制，故D选项（太有限而无法复制）是合理概括的正确选项。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A. 有助于解释人工智能：文中定位处并未提及相关内容

【曲解文意】B. 可能会对机器人制造造成误导：4段2句中提到，目前还没有好的理论来解释意识是什么，以及如何制造出一台达到人类意识水平的机器，可见对意识的认识会影响机器人的制造，但不一定会对其造成误导，故排除。

【偷换概念】C. 给流行的科幻电视连续剧带来灵感：3段2句中虽然出现sci-fi TV series，但该句意指科幻电视连续剧描绘了机器人能够像人类一样观察、行动和反应这样的想法，但并未提及我们对意识的认识可以给科幻电视连续剧带来灵感，且该选项与大卫的观点无关，故排除。
2019-Traditional Reading-3-2.tips:
这道题问的是David Eagleman对我们当前意识认知水平的看法。要答对，关键不是靠猜，而是回到原文找他说了什么。通常这类题只要锁定人名，就能快速定位到相关段落——这里就是文章第四段开头两句。

我们来看原文怎么说的：第一句就指出，“the human mind is far too complicated to be understood, let alone replicated”（人类的思维太过复杂，连理解都做不到，更别说复制了）。这句话已经非常直白地表达了态度：我们现在的理解程度远远不够，根本谈不上复制意识。接着第二句进一步补充说，“we don’t yet have a good theory of what consciousness even is, or how to build a machine that has it”（我们甚至还没有一个关于意识到底是什么的好理论，也不知道怎么造出有意识的机器）。这两句话合起来，核心意思就是：**认知太有限，复制不可能**。

现在看选项，D项说“is too limited for us to reproduce it”（太有限而无法复制），正好精准对应原文的“too complicated to be understood, let alone replicated”和“don’t yet have a good theory”。这不是字对字翻译，而是对作者观点的合理概括，所以D是正确答案。

其他选项为什么错？A项说“有助于解释人工智能”，但原文压根没提AI和意识知识之间的这种关系，纯属无中生有。B项说“可能误导机器人制造”，听起来有点道理，但仔细想想，原文说的是“我们还不知道怎么做”，而不是“我们的错误理解会带偏研发方向”——前者是能力不足，后者是方向错误，这是两回事，属于偷换问题性质。C项提到科幻剧，虽然前文确实出现了“sci-fi TV series”，但那是用来举例说明公众对机器人的幻想，并不是David Eagleman的观点，更没说现实中的意识研究启发了电视剧，所以也是张冠李戴。

【题目及选项概览】

The solution to the ethical issues brought by autonomous vehicles _______.

对于自动驾驶汽车带来的伦理问题，其解决办法_______。

A. can hardly ever be found.

   几乎无法找到

B. is still beyond our capacity.

   仍然超出我们的能力

C. causes little public concern.

   几乎没有引起公众的关注

D. has aroused much curiosity.

   已经激起了很多人的好奇心


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的关键词autonomous vehicles可以定位至5段2句，该句指出，自动驾驶车辆的投入使用会引发棘手的道德问题，该段剩余内容则对此进行具体阐述。3、4句提到人类驾驶汽车时有时需要瞬间做出决定，且其设计的东西多且复杂；5、6句指出，人工智能的”想象力“远不及人类的复杂，让其预测一切可能发生的驾驶场景是一项编程难题。由此可知，自动驾驶车辆引发的道德问题，解决起来很难，仍然超出我们的能力，故B选项（仍然超出我们的能力）为正确选项。

【过度推理】A. 几乎无法找到：根据本段内容，自动驾驶车辆引发的道德问题，解决起来很难，但并非无法找到解决办法，故排除A

【无中生有】C. 几乎没有引起公众的关注：在定位段落区间内并未提及。
【无中生有】D. 已经激起了很多人的好奇心：在定位段落区间内并未提及。
2019-Traditional Reading-3-3.tips:
这道题问的是“自动驾驶汽车带来的伦理问题的解决办法_______”，关键是要搞清楚作者在文中对这个问题持什么态度。我们先顺着题干里的关键词 autonomous vehicles 去原文找线索，很快就能定位到第五段。


第五段开头就说，自动驾驶汽车的上路会引发棘手的道德困境（thorny ethical dilemmas）。接下来几句话解释了为什么棘手：人在开车时，面对突发状况能靠直觉或经验快速做决定；但给人工智能编程时，却要预设所有可能的情形——而现实中的驾驶场景千变万化，根本没法穷尽。文中特别提到，AI 的“想象力”远不如人类复杂，这让程序员很难把所有道德判断都写进代码里。


从这些描述可以看出，作者并不是说这个问题完全无解（所以不能选 A 说“几乎无法找到”），而是强调目前的技术和认知水平还不足以应对这种复杂性。换句话说，我们还没有能力搞定它，这正好对应选项 B：“仍然超出我们的能力”。这个表述既承认了困难的存在，又没把话说死，非常符合原文语气。


至于 C 和 D，一个说“公众不太关心”，一个说“激起很多人好奇”，但通读第五段甚至全文，根本找不到关于公众反应的任何信息。这就是典型的无中生有——题目没提的事，再合理也不能选。考研阅读特别爱设这种陷阱，大家一定要记住：答案必须有原文依据，不能靠自己脑补。

【题目及选项概览】

The author’s attitude toward Google’s pledge is one of ________.

对于谷歌的承诺，作者持有_______的态度。

A. affirmation  肯定

B. skepticism  怀疑

C. contempt  轻视

D. respect  尊重


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的Google’s pledges可以定位至7段。该段在描述谷歌的承诺，即不会涉及和部署违反道德和法律的人工智能。但该段为事实的描述，无法体现作者观点，故还需要继续阅读8段。8段1句提到，尽管谷歌的这项声明含糊其辞，但它标志着一个起点。由此可见，作者对谷歌的承诺持有偏正想的积极态度。故A选项（肯定）为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】B. 怀疑/ C. 轻视：B选项以及C选项与原文表示的正向含义相反。
【过度推理】D. 尊重：8段1句中使用了vague（含糊其辞）来形容谷歌的承诺，因此可以得知，作者对谷歌的承诺并非全盘肯定，更不会达到尊重的程度，故排除。

我们先顺着题干里的关键词Google’s pledge去找原文。定位到第七段，确实详细讲了谷歌的承诺内容，但注意——这一整段都是在客观陈述事实，就像新闻报道一样，没有掺杂作者自己的看法。这时候千万别急着选答案！态度题的答案往往藏在事实之后的评价里。

所以作者的态度其实是有保留的肯定：他看到了问题（太模糊），但也认可这是迈向正确方向的第一步。这种“虽然……但是……”的结构在考研阅读中特别常见，后半句往往是作者真正想表达的观点。这时候再看选项，A项“affirmation”（肯定）就最贴切——它不要求全盘赞美，只要整体倾向是正面的就行。

Today the rapid growth of artificial intelligence ( AI ) raises fundamental questions :" What is intelligence , identity , or consciousness ?" What makes humans humans

What is being called artificial general intelligence , machines that would imitate the way humans think , continues to evade scientists . Yet humans remain fascinated by the idea of robots that would look , move, and respond like humans , similar to those recently depicted on popular sci-fi TV series such as " West world " and " Humans ".

Just how people think is still far too complex to be understood , let alone reproduced , says David Eagleman , a Stanford University neuroscientist . " We are just in a situation where there are no good theories explaining what consciousness actually is and how you could ever build a machine to get there ."

But that doesn’t mean crucial ethical issues involving AI aren’t at hand . The coming use of autonomous vehicles , for example , poses thorny ethical questions . Human drivers sometimes must make split-second decisions . Their reactions may be a complex combination of instant reflexes , input from past driving experiences , and what their eyes and ears tell them in that moment . AI " vision " today is not nearly as sophisticated as that of humans . And to anticipate every imaginable driving situation is a difficult programming problem .

Whenever decisions are based on masses of data , " you quickly get into a lot of ethical questions ," notes Tan Kiat How , chief executive of a Singapore-based agency that is helping the government develop a voluntary code for the ethical use of AI . Along with Singapore , other governments and mega-corporations are beginning to establish their own guidelines . Britain is setting up a data ethics center . India released its AI ethics strategy this spring .

On June 7 Google pledged not to " design or deploy AI " that would cause " overall harm ," or to develop AI-directed weapons or use AI for surveillance that would violate international norms . It also pledged not to deploy AI whose use would violate international laws or human rights .

While the statement is vague , it represents one starting point . So does the idea that decisions made by AI systems should be explainable , transparent , and fair .

To put it another way : How can we make sure that the thinking of intelligent machines reflects humanity ’s highest values Only then will they be useful servants and not Frankenstein ’s out-of-control monster .

【题目及选项概览】

Which of the following would be the best title for the text ?

以下哪个是本文的最佳标题？

A. AI’s Future:In the Hands of Tech Giants

   人工智能的未来：掌握在科技巨头手中

B. Frankenstein, the Novel Predicting the Age of AI

  《弗兰肯斯坦》，预测人工智能时代的小说

C. The Conscience of AI: Complex But Inevitable

   人工智能的良知：复杂而又不可避免

D. AI Shall Be Killers Once Out of Control

   人工智能一旦失控就会成为杀手


【定位及答案】

本题是主旨题，需要重点阅读文章的首末段与各段首末句，把握文章结构，进行解题。文章1段通过Mary Shelley的书引出“新技术所引发的道德问题”这一话题。2-4段提到人工智能引起的一些根本问题以及人工智能的发展现状。5段举例说明人工智能所引发的道德问题。6-8段具体说明了对人工智能所引发的道德问题的应对策略。9段指出只有确保智能机器的思维反映人类的最高价值观，人工智能才能为人类所用。由此可知，全文围绕人工智能引发的道德问题展开，强调这一问题是非常复杂的，但也是科技发展过程中不可避免的。故C选项（人工智能的良知：复杂而又不可避免）为正确选项。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A. 人工智能的未来：掌握在科技巨头的手中：文中并未提及Tech Giants 的相关信息，故排除。

【以偏概全】B.《弗兰肯斯坦》，预测人工智能时代的小说：1段2句表明《弗兰肯斯坦》这本小说预示了未来科技将会引起的道德问题，而非预测人工智能时代，且这一内容仅为文章的细节信息，并非全文讨论的主体，故排除。

【断章取义】D. 人工智能一旦失控就会成为杀手：9段指出，只有确保智能机器的思维能够反映人类的最高价值观，它们才能为人类所利用，而不是成为弗兰肯斯坦手下失控的怪物，可见，人工智能一旦失控可能成为怪物，但怪物不等于杀手，且只是文章的部分内容，不适于概括全文主旨。
2019-Traditional Reading-3-5.tips:
这道题问的是“以下哪个选项最适合作为文章的标题”，也就是要你抓住整篇文章的核心主旨。做这类题，千万别一上来就看选项猜答案，而是先快速回顾全文讲了什么——尤其是开头和结尾，因为作者通常会在那里亮出主要观点。

文章一开始提到玛丽·雪莱的小说《弗兰肯斯坦》，但这不是为了讲文学，而是用它作为一个引子，带出一个更深层的问题：当人类创造出强大的新技术（比如人工智能）时，随之而来的道德困境该怎么面对？接下来几段并没有大谈AI有多厉害或多危险，而是反复讨论一个问题：我们该如何给AI赋予“良知”？也就是说，AI该不该有道德判断？如果有，又该以谁的价值观为准？

特别值得注意的是，文章后半部分强调，虽然这个问题非常复杂——涉及技术、哲学、伦理等多个层面——但它又是科技发展过程中不可避免的一环。最后一段更是点明：只有让智能机器的“思维”体现人类最高的价值观，AI才能真正造福人类。这说明作者的态度不是恐慌或否定，而是理性地指出：道德问题虽难，但必须解决。

现在来看选项。A选项说“AI的未来掌握在科技巨头手中”，但通篇压根没提什么“科技巨头”，属于典型的无中生有，直接排除。B选项把重点放在《弗兰肯斯坦》“预测AI时代”上，可小说只是个开头的例子，全文重心根本不在文学预言，而是现实中的伦理挑战，所以这是以偏概全。D选项语气特别吓人，“AI一旦失控就会成为杀手”，听起来像电影剧情，但原文并没有渲染这种极端后果，反而强调通过价值观引导可以避免灾难，因此D属于过度推断+情绪化表述。

而C选项“人工智能的良知：复杂但是不可避免”正好精准概括了全文的核心——既点出了“良知”（即道德问题）这个关键词，又用“复杂但不可避免”呼应了作者对这一议题的理性态度。所以，这才是真正能覆盖全文主旨的标题。

小技巧提醒：选标题题最怕被某个细节或例子带跑偏。记住，正确选项往往不具体、不极端、不情绪化，而是能“罩住”整篇文章的中心思想。遇到像B、D这种听起来很抓眼球的选项，更要警惕——考研英语喜欢用它们当“烟雾弹”！

States will be able to force more people to pay sales tax when they make online purchase under a Supreme Court decision Thursday that will leave shoppers with lighter wallets but is a big financial win for states .

The Supreme Court ’s opinion Thursday overruled a pair of decades-old decisions that states said cost them billions of dollars in lost revenue annually . The decisions made it more difficult for states to collect sales tax on certain online purchases .

The cases the court overturned said that if a business was shipping a customer ’s purchase to a state where the business didn’t have a physical presence such as a warehouse or office , the business didn’t have to collect sales tax for the state . Customers were generally responsible for paying the sales tax to the state themselves if they weren’t charged it , but most didn’t realize they owed it and few paid .

Justice Anthony Kennedy wrote that the previous decisions were flawed . “ Each year the physical presence rule becomes further removed from economic reality and results in significant revenue losses to the States ,” he wrote in an opinion joined by four other justices . Kennedy wrote that the rule “ limited states ’ ability to seek long-term prosperity and has prevented market participants from competing on an even playing field .”

The ruling is a victory for big chains with a presence in many states , since they usually collect sales tax on online purchases already . Now , rivals will be charging sales tax where they hadn’t before . Big chains have been collecting sales tax nationwide because they typically have physical stores in whatever state a purchase is being shipped to . Amazon.com , with its network of warehouses , also collects sales tax in every state that charges it , though third-party sellers who use the site don’t have to .

Until now , many sellers that have a physical presence in only a single state or a few states have been able to avoid charging sales tax es when they ship to addresses outside those states . Sellers that use eBay and Etsy , which provide platforms for smaller sellers , also haven’t been collecting sales tax nationwide . Under the ruling Thursday , states can pass laws requiring out-of-state sellers to collect the state ’s sales tax from customers and send it to the state .

Retail trade groups praised the ruling , saying it levels the playing field for local and online businesses . The losers , said retail analyst Neil Saunders , are online-only retailers , especially smaller ones . Those retailers may face headaches complying with various state sales tax laws . The Small Business & Entrepreneurship Council advocacy group said in a statement , “ Small businesses and internet entrepreneurs are not well served at all by this decision .”

【题目及选项概览】

The Supreme Court decision Thursday will ________.

最高法院周四的裁定将________。

A. better business’ relations with states

   改善企业与各州之间的关系

B. put most online business in a dilemma

   使大多数线上企业进退两难

C. make more online shoppers pay sales tax

   迫使更多网络购物者缴纳销售税

D. force some states to cut sales tax

   迫使一些州削减销售税


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的关键词Supreme Court 和 Thursday可以定位至1段，该段提到，根据美国最高法院周四做出的一项裁定，美国各州将能有权要求更多的人在网上购物时缴纳销售税，C选项（迫使更多网络购物者缴纳销售税）为同意替换选项。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A. 改善企业与各州之间的关系：定位部分并未提及企业和各州之间的关系是否有所改善，故排除。

【无中生有】B. 使大多数线上企业进退两难：定位部分并未提及对企业的影响。

【反向干扰】D. 迫使一些州削减销售税：1段可知，美国最高法院的裁定赋予了州政府征收更多销售税的权利，而非迫使一些州削减销售税，D属于反向干扰，排除。
2019-Traditional Reading-4-1.tips:
这道题问的是“最高法院周四的裁定将________”，关键是要搞清楚这个裁定到底带来了什么直接影响。我们先别急着看选项，而是回到原文找线索。题干里有两个非常明确的定位词——“Supreme Court”和“Thursday”，这两个词一出现，基本就能锁定文章第一段。


第一段开头就说，根据最高法院周四的一项裁决，各州现在有权要求更多人在网上购物时缴纳销售税。这句话就是解题的“金钥匙”。注意这里说的是“more online shoppers pay sales tax”，也就是更多网购消费者要交税，而不是说企业怎么办、州政府要不要减税。所以正确答案必须紧扣这个核心意思。


再来看选项C：“make more online shoppers pay sales tax”（迫使更多网络购物者缴纳销售税），这几乎就是原文那句话的同义转述，只不过把“allow states to require”换成了“make...pay”，意思完全一致。考研英语阅读特别喜欢考这种“换汤不换药”的表达，只要你能识别出语义对应，就能稳稳选对。


其他几个选项为什么不对？A选项说“改善企业与各州的关系”，但原文压根没提企业跟州政府之间关系变好还是变坏，纯属凭空想象，属于典型的无中生有陷阱。B选项说“让大多数线上企业进退两难”，听起来好像有道理，但第一段根本没讨论对企业的影响——哪怕后文提到了，这道题问的是“裁定将……”，而裁定的直接对象是消费者缴税问题，不是企业困境，所以不能选。D选项更离谱，说“迫使一些州削减销售税”，可原文明明说州政府现在可以收更多税，方向完全相反，这是典型的反向干扰，一定要警惕。


做这类题有个小技巧：**题干问的是“裁定将……”，那就优先找裁定带来的最直接、最明确的结果**，别被选项里看似合理但原文没说的“延伸影响”带偏。尤其是A、B这种涉及“企业”的选项，很容易让人联想到现实中的电商税问题，但考研阅读只认原文证据，不认常识推测。记住：**有依据才选，没提到就排除**。

【题目及选项概览】

It can be learned from paragraphs 2 and 3 that the overruled decisions ________.

从第2,3段可知，遭到推翻的裁定________。

A. have led to the dominance of e-commerce

   已经使电子商务处于主导地位

B. have cost consumers a lot over the years

   近年来消费者花费巨大

C. were widely criticized by online purchasers

   受到网络购物者的广泛批判

D. were considered unfavorable by states

   被各州认为是不利的


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的段落信息提示，可以定位至文章的2、3段。2段主要描述了被推翻的旧决议在州政府眼中的弊端：每年让各州损失数十亿美元的税收收入，同时加大了各州对某些网购商品征收销售税的难度。3段继续介绍了旧决议的基本内容以及消极影响，即企业可以合理的免于为各州向顾客代收销售税，且很少有顾客会主动向州政府缴税。由此可以推断，被推翻的旧决议对于州政府而言是不利的，故D选项（被各州认为是不利的）是正确选项。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A. 已经使电子商务处于主导地位：文中定位区间并未提及有关电子商务处于主导地位的信息，故排除。

【反向干扰】B. 近年来使消费者花费巨大：根据2、3段内容，旧决议加大了各州对某些网购商品征收销售税的难度，且大多数顾客没有意识到自己已经欠税，并且极少有人主动交税，由此可知，旧决议其实在近年来为消费者生了不少钱。故为反向干扰，排除。

【无中生有】C. 受到网络购物者的广泛批判：文中定位区间并未提及网络购物者的态度，且根据文中内容推测，旧决议为网购者省钱，所以应该不会受到他们的广泛批评。
2019-Traditional Reading-4-2.tips:
这道题问的是：从文章第2段和第3段可以了解到，那些被推翻的裁定（overruled decisions）怎么样了？我们要做的，就是回到这两段里找线索，看看作者是怎么评价这些旧规定的。


先看第2段。里面提到，这些旧裁定让各州每年损失数十亿美元的税收，而且让州政府很难对某些网购商品收销售税。换句话说，这些规定对州政府来说是个“坑”——钱收不上来，财政受影响。再看第3段，它解释了为什么收不上税：根据旧规则，企业不用替各州向顾客代收销售税，而消费者自己又很少主动去交这笔税。结果就是，州政府眼睁睁看着钱溜走，却没办法。


把这些信息串起来，就能明白：这些被推翻的裁定，在各州看来显然是不利的。它们不仅造成财政损失，还削弱了州政府征税的能力。所以选项D说“被各州认为是不利的”，完全符合原文意思。


再来看看其他选项为什么不对。A选项说这些裁定“让电商占据主导地位”——但原文根本没提电商是否因此变强或主导市场，纯属脑补，典型的“无中生有”。B选项说“让消费者花了很多钱”，可实际情况恰恰相反：因为没交销售税，消费者可能还省了钱，只是他们不知道自己其实欠着税。所以B不仅没依据，还跟文意反着来。C选项说“被网购用户广泛批评”，但文中只说消费者很少主动缴税，并没说他们反对这些裁定，更谈不上“广泛批评”，又是凭空想象。


做这类题有个小技巧：当题干提到具体段落时，一定要紧扣那几段的内容，别被自己对现实的了解带偏。比如你可能觉得电商确实强大，或者消费者被多收费了，但只要原文没写，就不能选。另外，注意区分“谁受益、谁受损”——这里明显是州政府受损，而不是消费者或企业，抓住这个主体，答案就清晰多了。

根据题干关键词Justice Anthony Kennedy以及physical presence rule可以定位至4段，4段3句中提到，大法官安东尼·肯尼迪称，对实体店实行的规定限制了各州寻求长期繁荣的能力，并妨碍了市场参与者们的公平竞争（has prevented market participants from competing on an even playing field)，C选项（损害了公平的市场竞争）是该部分的同意替换选项。


【错选分析】

【过度推理】A. 阻碍了经济发展：4段中2、3句提到，对实体点进行的规定给各州带来了巨大的税收损失，限制了各州寻求长期繁荣的能力，可见该规定造成了不良影响，但不意味着其阻碍了经济发展，A属于过度推理。

【反向干扰】B. 给国家带来了繁荣：由上述文章分析可知，其妨碍了公平竞争，限制了寻求长期繁荣的能力，而非带来了繁荣，故排除。

【反向干扰】D. 促进了各州税收收入的增长：与文章表意内容相反。
2019-Traditional Reading-4-3.tips:
这道题问的是大法官安东尼·肯尼迪对“实体店存在规则”（physical presence rule）的看法。我们要做的，就是回到原文中找到他具体说了什么，而不是靠自己的想象去猜。


根据题干中的关键词Justice Anthony Kennedy和physical presence rule，我们可以快速定位到文章第四段。这一段里提到，肯尼迪大法官认为，这个规则“has prevented market participants from competing on an even playing field”——也就是说，它让市场上的参与者没法在公平的条件下竞争。这句话非常关键，直接对应了选项C：“损害了公平的市场竞争”。


这里有个解题小技巧：考研英语阅读中，正确选项往往是对原文某句话的同义转述，而不是字面照搬。比如原文说“competing on an even playing field”（在公平的赛场上竞争），选项就用“fair market competition”（公平的市场竞争）来表达同一个意思，这就是典型的同意替换。


再来看其他选项为什么不对。A选项说“阻碍了经济发展”，听起来好像也有道理，因为原文确实提到这个规则给各州带来了税收损失、限制了长期繁荣能力。但注意！“限制某州财政能力”不等于“阻碍整个国家的经济发展”——这是典型的以偏概全或过度推断。考研阅读最忌讳自己脑补，一切要以原文明确信息为准。


B选项说“给国家带来繁荣”，明显和肯尼迪批评该规则的态度相悖，直接排除。D选项说“促进了各州税收增长”，而原文恰恰说的是相反情况——这个规则导致各州损失了大量税收，所以D也是反着来的错误选项。


总结一下：做这类细节题，关键是精准定位+忠实理解。不要被看似合理的干扰项带跑，尤其要警惕那些“好像说得通”但原文没明确说的选项。记住，正确答案一定能在原文中找到直接依据，而C选项正是如此。

States will be able to force more people to pay sales tax when they make online purchase under a Supreme Court decision Thursday that will leave shoppers with lighter wallets but is a big financial win for states .

The Supreme Court ’s opinion Thursday overruled a pair of decades-old decisions that states said cost them billions of dollars in lost revenue annually . The decisions made it more difficult for states to collect sales tax on certain online purchases .

The cases the court overturned said that if a business was shipping a customer ’s purchase to a state where the business didn’t have a physical presence such as a warehouse or office , the business didn’t have to collect sales tax for the state . Customers were generally responsible for paying the sales tax to the state themselves if they weren’t charged it , but most didn’t realize they owed it and few paid .

Justice Anthony Kennedy wrote that the previous decisions were flawed . “ Each year the physical presence rule becomes further removed from economic reality and results in significant revenue losses to the States ,” he wrote in an opinion joined by four other justices . Kennedy wrote that the rule “ limited states ’ ability to seek long-term prosperity and has prevented market participants from competing on an even playing field .”

The ruling is a victory for big chains with a presence in many states , since they usually collect sales tax on online purchases already . Now , rivals will be charging sales tax where they hadn’t before . Big chains have been collecting sales tax nationwide because they typically have physical stores in whatever state a purchase is being shipped to . Amazon.com , with its network of warehouses , also collects sales tax in every state that charges it , though third-party sellers who use the site don’t have to .

Until now , many sellers that have a physical presence in only a single state or a few states have been able to avoid charging sales tax es when they ship to addresses outside those states . Sellers that use eBay and Etsy , which provide platforms for smaller sellers , also haven’t been collecting sales tax nationwide . Under the ruling Thursday , states can pass laws requiring out-of-state sellers to collect the state ’s sales tax from customers and send it to the state .

Retail trade groups praised the ruling , saying it levels the playing field for local and online businesses . The losers , said retail analyst Neil Saunders , are online-only retailers , especially smaller ones . Those retailers may face headaches complying with various state sales tax laws . The Small Business & Entrepreneurship Council advocacy group said in a statement , “ Small businesses and internet entrepreneurs are not well served at all by this decision .”

【题目及选项概览】

Who are most likely to welcome the Supreme Court ruling ？

谁有可能欢迎最高法院的此次裁定？

A. Internet entrepreneurs

   互联网企业家

B. Big-chain owners

   大型连锁企业的老板

C. Third-party sellers

   第三方卖家

D. Small retailers

   小型零售商


【定位及答案】

根据题干定位词welcome the Supreme Court ruling可以定位至5段；5段1句中提到，最高法院的裁决对大型连锁企业来说是一个胜利；3句中提到，大型连锁企业一直在全国范围内对商品征收销售税，由此可知，大型连锁企业的老板从最新的裁决中收益较多，因此最有可能支持最高法院的裁决，故B选项（大型连锁企业的老板）为正确选项。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A. 互联网企业家：7段4句中提到，这个裁决对小型企业和互联网企业家毫无益处，由此可知该裁决不会受到这两者的欢迎，故排除。

【反向干扰】C. 第三方买家：5段4句中提到，使用亚马逊平台的第三方卖家不需要征收销售税，表明最高法院的裁决对第三方卖家影响不大，因此他们支持这个裁决的概率也不大，故排除。
【反向干扰】D. 小型零售商：7段4句中提到，这个裁决对小型企业和互联网企业家毫无益处，由此可知该裁决不会受到这两者的欢迎，故排除。
2019-Traditional Reading-4-4.tips:
这道题问的是“谁最有可能欢迎最高法院的这项裁决”，关键在于找出文章中明确表达“支持”或“受益于”该裁决的群体。我们先别急着看选项，而是回到原文找线索——通常这种“态度题”都会在某一段直接点明某方是“赢家”或“受益者”。

文章第5段开头就给出了重要信息：“The Supreme Court’s decision is a victory for big-chain owners.” 这句话非常直白——最高法院的裁决对大型连锁企业老板来说是一场胜利。既然是“胜利”，那他们当然会欢迎这个结果。而且后面还补充说，这些大企业already collect sales tax nationwide（早已在全国范围内征收销售税），所以新裁决并没有增加他们的负担，反而让那些原本不用收税的线上小卖家也得照章办事，等于帮大企业拉平了竞争环境。

再来看其他选项为什么不对。A选项“互联网企业家”和D选项“小型零售商”其实可以一起看，因为文章第7段明确说：“The ruling is no help to small businesses or online entrepreneurs.” 意思是这项裁决对小企业和互联网创业者毫无帮助，那他们自然不会欢迎，直接排除A和D。

至于C选项“第三方卖家”，很多人可能会被“亚马逊上的卖家”这个概念迷惑。但注意第5段提到：“Third-party sellers on Amazon don’t have to collect sales tax.” 这说明他们在这次裁决前本来就不收税，而新规则主要针对的是像亚马逊自营这类大型在线零售商。虽然未来政策可能变化，但文章并未说第三方卖家因此受益，反而暗示他们可能面临更复杂的税务要求。所以他们不太可能是“最欢迎”的群体。

总结一下，解这类题有个小技巧：**找情感色彩强烈的词**，比如“victory”（胜利）、“help”（帮助）、“burden”（负担）等。谁被描述成“赢了”或“轻松了”，谁就最可能欢迎这个决定。而大型连锁企业老板正是那个被作者明确称为“胜利者”的角色，所以答案选B。

【题目及选项概览】

In dealing with the Supreme Court decision Thursday, the author ______.

在论述最高法院周四的裁定时，作者______。

A.gives a factual account of it and discusses its consequences

   给出了事实说明并讨论其影响

B.describes the long and complicated process of its making

   描述了其漫长而复杂的制定过程

C.presents its main points with conflicting views on them

   用相互矛盾的观点陈述其要领

D.cites some cases related to it and analyzes their implications

   列举了一些与此相关的案例，并分析了它们的影响


【定位及答案】

根据题干内容“在论述最高法院周四做出的裁决时，作者…”，结合周四裁决频繁在文中各个部分出现可以推断，该题目为宏观类型的题目，需要梳理文章整体结构。本文1-4段介绍了这项最新裁决，以及被否决的旧裁决及其缺陷。5-7段分别阐述了新裁决对大型连锁企业及竞争对手、各州政府、以及其它相关企业的影响。综上所述，A选项（给出了事实说明并讨论其影响）为正确选项。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】B. 描述了其漫长而复杂的制定过程：文中未提及裁决的置顶过程，故排除。

【无中生有】C. 用相互矛盾的观点陈述其要领：5-7段中虽然提到新裁决之下有一些赢家也有输家，但是这只能说明新裁决不是对所有组织都有利，且所用篇幅较少，故排除。

【无中生有】D. 列举了一些与此相关的案例，并分析了它们的影响：文中在阐述新裁决的相关影响时，简单列绝了一些案例，但并未就案例本身所造成的影响进行分析，故排除。
2019-Traditional Reading-4-5.tips:
这道题问的是作者在谈论最高法院周四的裁决时，采取了怎样的写作方式。要答对这种题，不能只盯着某一段看，得从整篇文章的结构入手，看看作者是怎么组织内容的。

通读全文你会发现，文章开头几段（比如第1到第4段）其实是在客观陈述这个裁决的基本事实：最高法院推翻了之前的某个旧判例，并解释了为什么那个旧判例有问题。这部分没有掺杂太多主观情绪，就是把事情说清楚——这对应选项里说的“factual account”（事实性描述）。

接着往下看，从第5段开始，作者话锋一转，开始分析这个裁决会带来什么后果：比如对大型零售商是利好，对小商家可能造成压力，各州政府现在可以收更多税，甚至影响到电商行业的整体格局。这些内容明显是在讨论裁决的后续影响和实际意义，也就是选项A里提到的“discusses its consequences”。

再来看其他选项为啥不对。B选项说作者描述了裁决“漫长而复杂的制定过程”，但文章压根没讲法官们怎么开会、怎么辩论、花了多长时间——这些细节完全没出现，属于典型的无中生有。C选项提到“用相互矛盾的观点陈述要点”，可实际上作者并没有摆出正反两方激烈争论的样子，而是以一种相对中立、分析性的语气展开，所以也不对。D选项说“列举相关案例并分析其影响”，但文中并没有具体讲某个案子（比如某某诉某某案），只是泛泛谈到行业或州政府层面的变化，所以这个选项也站不住脚。

这里提醒大家一个常见陷阱：遇到问“作者态度”或“写作手法”的题，千万别被某一段的情绪带偏。一定要通观全文结构，看看开头讲什么、中间分析什么、结尾有没有总结或预测。考研英语阅读特别喜欢考这种“整体把握能力”，而不是抠字眼。

所以综合来看，只有A选项准确概括了作者的写作思路：先讲清楚裁决本身是什么，再分析它会带来哪些连锁反应，既客观又深入，完全符合文章的实际内容。
